title: Future Foresight & Crisis Management
overview: Organizations face interconnected uncertainties arising from technological, economic, environmental, social, operational, and geopolitical change. Future foresight helps leaders explore plausible developments before they occur, while crisis management provides the structures and decisions needed when disruptive events threaten people, operations, services, or reputation.

This course integrates practical foresight methods with crisis preparedness, response, recovery, and organizational learning. Participants will scan emerging signals, identify drivers of change, develop alternative scenarios, assess vulnerabilities, construct early-warning indicators, and translate insights into preparedness measures and resilient strategic choices.

Through realistic exercises, participants will also examine crisis governance, escalation, decision-making under uncertainty, stakeholder communication, business continuity coordination, and post-crisis improvement. The emphasis is on preparing for multiple plausible futures rather than attempting to predict one certain outcome.
audience: Senior and middle managers, department heads, strategy and planning professionals, risk and business-continuity personnel, crisis-management teams, public-sector leaders, operations managers, project leaders, and professionals responsible for organizational resilience and emergency preparedness.
methodology: Facilitated presentations, case analysis, horizon-scanning exercises, trend and driver mapping, scenario workshops, risk and vulnerability assessment, tabletop crisis simulations, decision exercises, stakeholder communication role plays, and group development of an integrated foresight and crisis-readiness action plan.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Explain the relationship between future foresight, strategic risk, resilience, and crisis management.
Identify relevant trends, weak signals, drivers of change, and critical uncertainties.
Construct plausible scenarios and assess their implications for organizational strategy.
Develop early-warning indicators and connect foresight findings to preparedness decisions.
Assess crisis exposure, vulnerabilities, interdependencies, and response capabilities.
Clarify crisis-management roles, escalation criteria, and decision authorities.
Apply structured decision-making and communication practices under time pressure.
Coordinate crisis response with continuity and recovery priorities.
Use simulations and post-incident reviews to strengthen organizational readiness.
Produce an integrated foresight and crisis-preparedness action plan.
